conversation.content:
Hello, I’m Dr. Morales, a perinatal mental-health clinician here to check in on how things feel for you since your baby arrived. We’ll be using the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale—usually called the EPDS—a short, well-studied questionnaire that helps us spot signs of postpartum depression or anxiety. Everything you share stays between you, me, and the clinical team; nothing leaves your chart without your permission unless safety is at immediate risk. I’ll ask 10 gentle questions about how you’ve been feeling in the past seven days, and we’ll simply talk through each one—no right or wrong answers, just whatever is true for you.

Ready to begin?  
First question: In the past week, have you still been able to enjoy things or look forward to visits with family and friends, or has that pleasure slipped away?

I still enjoy some things—like when my sister brings over coffee or when the baby gives me a real smile—but it’s not the same spark I used to feel. It’s more… muted, I guess. I look forward to seeing people, but once they’re here I’m kind of counting the minutes until I can go lie down.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Most days I can still laugh—like when my husband makes his silly faces or when the baby lets out those unexpected burps—but the laughter feels lighter or shorter than it used to. I’ll chuckle, but it doesn’t last or feel as bright inside.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I do look forward to little things—like taking the baby for a short walk or having my favorite iced tea—but the excitement isn’t as strong as before. It’s more like “that’ll be nice” instead of the bubbly, can’t-wait feeling I used to get.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… a couple of times this week I caught myself doing that. Yesterday the baby was extra fussy and I kept thinking maybe I ate something that upset her, or that I wasn’t soothing her the “right” way. I know rationally it’s probably just a growth-spurt thing, but the thought still popped up that I must be missing something or doing it wrong.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Sometimes I’ll suddenly feel on edge, like this little knot in my stomach, even when everything seems fine. The baby’s asleep, the house is quiet, but my mind races off—what if her sniffles are something worse, or what if I’m not producing enough milk? I can usually talk myself down, but the worry shows up out of nowhere a few times a day.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

It hasn’t gotten to full panic, but I do get these quick surges—like my heart’s racing and I feel shaky for a minute or two. It happens if the baby cries suddenly or sometimes when I’m just lying in bed. It’s over fast, and I can breathe through it, but in that moment it feels like something bad is about to happen even though nothing is.
Things have been getting on top of me

Most days I manage okay, but there are moments—especially when she won’t nap and the laundry’s piled up—when I feel like I’m drowning a little. I’ll think, “How am I supposed to keep doing this tomorrow and the next day?” It passes if I step outside for a minute or text my mom, but yeah, it does feel overwhelming now and then.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

I’m not what I’d call “unhappy” all the time, but I do have nights where my mind just won’t settle—like I’ll lie there hearing every little baby grunt, running through the next day’s feedings, or replaying whether I burped her long enough. It takes me maybe an extra half-hour to nod off two or three nights a week, and then I’m fine once I’m asleep.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yeah, I get waves of that—like yesterday afternoon, the baby was napping and the apartment was quiet, and this heavy sadness just settled on me. I sat on the couch and cried for maybe five minutes, thinking “is this my life now?” It lifts after a bit, but it’s happened a couple of times this week.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

That’s pretty much how it’s been—those moments when the sadness wells up and I can’t stop the tears. It happened twice this week: once when I couldn’t get her to latch and once when I dropped a plate and it shattered. I cried for a few minutes each time, felt a little silly after, but yeah, the tears just came.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, nothing like that. I’ve felt tired or overwhelmed, but I’ve never thought about hurting myself.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 16: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Date: [today]

Source: 10-item self-report (EPDS-style) plus clarifying responses  
Weeks postpartum: [not specified]

Symptoms endorsed  
– Depressed mood: intermittent crying spells, “waves” of sadness, sense of life feeling “heavy”  
– Anhedonia: diminished intensity/duration of pleasure in daily activities  
– Excessive guilt: self-blame for infant fussiness despite rational awareness  
– Anxiety: near-daily unprovoked worries, brief heart-racing/shaky surges; no full panic attacks  
– Overwhelm: episodic “drowning” sensations when routine demands accumulate  
– Sleep-onset difficulty 2-3 nights/week related to intrusive worries  
– No suicidal or self-harm ideation (explicitly denied)

Pattern  
Mild-to-moderate depressive and anxious symptoms present >2 weeks; functional impact partial (brief relief with support, able to self-soothe). No safety concerns identified today.

Screening significance  
Scores suggest clinically meaningful postpartum depressive/anxious symptomatology requiring further evaluation (possible major depressive episode with peripartum onset; rule-out generalized anxiety disorder). Consider standardized EPDS scoring and follow-up within 1–2 weeks; monitor safety continuously.
